extracted.intended_audience: writers, conversationalists, and stage actors / literate public interested in literary criticism and performance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on making stories and stage performances effective: using surprise and probability in narration, style choices in poetry and prose, and specific rules for pronunciation, vocal tone, and gesture in acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise as the life of stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprize is so much the Life of Stories, that every one aims at it, who endeavours to please by telling them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a turn of surprise to command attention, strike with sudden passion, or occasion laughter; surprise often matters more than elegant phrasing or arrangement for long-commanding attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautifying graces are subordinate
rubrics_metrics.description: Smooth Delivery, an elegant Choice of Words, and a sweet Arrangement, are all beautifying Graces, but not the particulars in this Point of Conversation which either long command the Attention, or strike with the Violence of a sudden Passion, or occasion the burst of Laughter which accompanies Humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish of language and order improve a tale but cannot substitute for an effective surprising turn or genuine emotional force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain probability; avoid outraging truth
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a Set of Men who outrage Truth, instead of affecting us with a Manner in telling it; who over-leap the Line of Probability, that they may be seen to move out of the common Road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice credibility for the sake of startling the audience. Excessive improbability or invented wonders ('a kind of Nonsense against the Philosophy of Nature') undermines esteem and often produces scorn rather than admiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid measuring character by extravagant anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: His endeavour to glory at their Expence becomes a Ground of Quarrel, and the Scorn and Indifference with which they entertain it begins the immediate Punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boastful or extravagant storytellers who try to raise their character by implausible tales risk being met with silence, scorn, or indifference; such social reactions wound more deeply than direct contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social correction of improbable talk: silence as a tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The first of these is a general Silence, which I would not advise any one to interpret in his own behalf. It is often the Effect of Prudence in avoiding a Quarrel... and but very seldom the Effect of Weakness in believing suddenly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When encountering an implausible storyteller, a deliberate silence or negligent indifference signals contempt and can curb the practice without escalating into argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social correction of improbable talk: expose by imitation/exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: The other Method ... is to over-shoot such Talkers in their own Bow, or to raise the Story with further Degrees of Impossibility, and set up for a Voucher to them in such a manner as must let them see they stand detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer absurd claims by parodying or exaggerating them further (mimicry), causing the teller to see the absurdity and feel shame; this 'mimickry' can be an effective corrective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of persona/letter-characters to vary writing
rubrics_metrics.description: I often chuse this way of casting my Thoughts into a Letter ... because it gave me an Opportunity of introducing a great variety of Characters into my Work, which could not have been done, had I always written in the Person of the Spectator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting different correspondent voices (fictional personae) is a deliberate device to diversify material and perspectives in periodical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory should fit and elucidate virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Spencer's general Plan is the Representation of six Virtues... The six Personages are supposed under proper Allegories suitable to their respective Characters, to do all that is necessary for the full Manifestation of the respective Virtues which they are to exert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using allegory, map characters and episodes appropriately to the virtues or ideas they represent so the allegory clarifies rather than confuses (examples: Red-cross Knight for Christian life; Britomart for chastity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid puns, forced antitheses, and affected wit in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: His stile is very Poetical; no Puns, Affectations of Wit, forced Antitheses, or any of that low Tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sincere poetic diction and avoid cheap rhetorical tricks; use well-chosen words and exquisite measures ('numbers') rather than contrived cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of apt and varied epithets and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Homer's Epithets were much admired by Antiquity: See what great Justness and Variety there is in these Epithets of the Trees ... The sailing Pine, the Cedar proud and tall, The Vine-prop Elm ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ precise, varied, and appropriate epithets and images to enhance description and give striking, memorable detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of art: assist action to represent nature (naturalness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Design of Art is to assist Action as much as possible in the Representation of Nature; for the Appearance of Reality is that which moves us in all Representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for naturalness in performance: artifice should support, not replace, believable expression; the closer to nature, the greater the force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match vocal tone to the emotion expressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature herself has assigned to every Emotion of the Soul, its peculiar Cast of the Countenance, Tone of Voice, and Manner of Gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the following vocal qualities as appropriate to emotions (examples from the text): anger — acute, raised, hurrying; sorrow/complaint — flexible, slow, interrupted, mournful; fear — low, hesitating, abject; courage — louder, full; pleasure — luxurious, mild, tender, joyous; perplexity — grave, earnest, uniform (see quoted passages from Lear, Wolsey, Lady Macbeth, Don Sebastian, Caius Marius, Hamlet for models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Let action follow and enforce the voice
rubrics_metrics.description: As all these Varieties of Voice are to be directed by the Sense, so the Action is to be directed by the Voice, and with a beautiful Propriety, as it were to enforce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate gestures, posture, and movement with vocal delivery: raise/extend the arm, use the hand to lead or follow words, stamp the foot for contention or command; action should underline and reinforce speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face and eyes are the epitome of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The Face is the Epitome of the whole Man, and the Eyes are as it were the Epitome of the Face; ... the best Judges among the Romans were not extremely pleased, even with Roscius himself in his Masque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give priority to facial expression and eye movement—vary looks (steadfast, careless, sudden regard, joyful sparkle) to mark emotions; avoid fixed, immobile gazes that make an actor an 'absent Actor.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Govern facial and gestural variety with judgment (avoid buffoonery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not that the Form of the Face is to be shifted on every Occasion, lest it turn to Farce and Buffoonery; but it is certain that the Eyes have a wonderful Power of marking the Emotions of the Mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use changes of countenance and gesture judiciously—too frequent or uncontrolled shifts become farce; balance variety with propriety to avoid turning a serious scene into buffoonery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action as a universal tongue for broad comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is a kind of Universal Tongue; all Men are subject to the same Passions, and consequently know the same Marks of them in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on expressive action to communicate across audiences and language barriers; gestures and facial signs convey emotion even where words may not be fully understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good sense is necessary for good acting
rubrics_metrics.description: I venture to lay it down as a Maxim, that without Good Sense no one can be a good Player, and that he is very unfit to personate the Dignity of a Roman Hero, who cannot enter into the Rules for Pronunciation and Gesture delivered by a Roman Orator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors must possess intelligence and understanding of rhetorical/psychological principles; mechanical skill alone is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch and compass of the voice must be controlled
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Voice ... has its particular Medium and Compass, and the Sweetness of Speech consists in leading it through all the Variety of Tones naturally, and without touching any Extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find and sustain the natural median pitch and range for the voice; lead the voice through tonal variety without resorting to extremes. Practice to maintain pitch (anecdote: Gracchus used a pipe to check pitch) but internalize the sense of that control.
